questions.q: What can you do from the DAGs list page's filter chips?
options: Jump straight to seeing which DAGs are Failed, Queued, Running, or Succeeded across the whole environment
Edit the Python source of a DAG directly
Permanently delete a DAG's run history
Change a task's operator type
questions.explain: The filter chips (All/Failed/Queued/Running/Success/Required Actions) let you triage status across every DAG at once, before opening any single one.

questions.q: In the Grid view, what does one column represent, and what does one row represent?
options: One column is one DAG run; one row is one task
One column is one task; one row is one user
Columns and rows both represent the same thing: DAGs
One column is a Python file; one row is a database table
questions.explain: The Grid view stacks every DAG run as a column and every task as a row, with a status cell at each intersection.

questions.q: How would you tell whether a specific task is flaky (fails intermittently) versus consistently broken, using the Grid view?
options: Read across that task's row and look at how its status cell changes (or doesn't) from run to run
There is no way to tell this from the Grid view
Check the DAGs list page instead — the Grid view can't show this
Only the Code tab can answer this question
questions.explain: Reading across a task's row shows its status across every run, which reveals whether failures are consistent or intermittent.

questions.q: What does the Calendar tab show that a run-by-run view would bury?
options: Patterns in outcomes across a full month, like a DAG that always fails on a specific day
The exact source code of the DAG
A list of every user who has access to the DAG
The DAG's dependency graph
questions.explain: The Calendar tab plots run outcomes across a month, surfacing recurring patterns that individual runs wouldn't show on their own.

questions.q: What does the Code tab display?
options: The exact Python source that produced the DAG, version by version
A live video of the DAG running
Only the DAG's schedule, nothing else
The SQL queries a task executed
questions.explain: The Code tab shows the actual Python source behind the DAG you're viewing, tracked across versions.
